description: Welcome to Team Astro-saur! We’re tackling the Space Mission Design Game challenge and looking for passionate builders to help us create an engaging, interactive space exploration experience. If you have skills in game development, coding, hardware, VR, or data visualization, join us and let's build something out of this world!
summary:
Astro SAUR: Mars Rescue is a browser-based space mission game for one or two players sharing a laptop. Players design a rescue mission, build a rocket, equip their rovers, study distress reports, and choose a landing site and communications orbit before travelling to Mars.

The goal is to rescue three stranded explorers, transmit a science report, and return safely to Earth. Each player controls an independent rover, managing battery power and rescue seats while working toward shared objectives. Short rescue quizzes introduce real Mars facts, with explanations and opportunities to retry.

The game makes engineering trade-offs visible: better equipment can increase capability but also adds mass, cost, power consumption, or data. Players learn through building, exploring, and reviewing their mission results.

Our fictional rescue scenario uses simplified mission calculations to make space engineering approachable and enjoyable. The game runs locally in a browser without installation and was developed with AI-assisted coding.
details:
Astro SAUR: Mars Rescue is an educational 2D browser game in which one or two players plan and complete a fictional mission to rescue three stranded explorers on Mars.

Players complete four preparation tasks: configure the rocket, equip the rovers, read distress reports, and choose a landing site and communications orbit. Their choices affect budget, payload mass, fuel, battery capacity, rescue seating, and scientific capability. The game checks whether the design fits the selected launch vehicle and leaves enough fuel to return home.

On Mars, players drive independent rovers using WASD and E for Player 1, and arrow keys and Enter for Player 2. Split-screen views allow them to explore separately while working toward shared goals. Players answer short educational questions to rescue explorers, collect observations at science sites, and transmit reports during communications windows. Questions pause the mission and provide feedback, allowing players to learn without losing resources.

Success requires bringing all three explorers safely to the rocket, transmitting at least one science report, and returning to Earth. A mission report evaluates rescue success, science, budget efficiency, and remaining time.

The game was built using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Canvas, with ChatGPT assistance for coding and debugging. It runs in a desktop browser without additional software. NASA resources informed the Mars facts; the rescue story, mission times, resource values, and orbital mechanics are simplified for gameplay.

Our aim is to make mission engineering accessible through exploration and cooperation. Instead of only reading about trade-offs, players experience how their design decisions affect the mission.

To play the submitted file, download the HTML file from the Project link and open it in Chrome or Edge.
